newsitem.title: USA: Fortsmann says to emerge from Chapter 11 in summer.
newsitem.headline: Fortsmann says to emerge from Chapter 11 in summer.

text.p: Forstmann & Co Inc, the woolen and worsted fabrics maker that sought protection from creditors in September 1995, said Tuesday it expects to emerge from Chapter 11 bankruptcy proceedings this summer.

Robert Dangremond, president and chief executive officer of the company, made the prediction as Forstmann said it had filed a plan of reorganization and disclosure statement with a federal bankruptcy court here.
The company said it hopes to schedule a court hearing on its disclosure statement in mid-May.
Once the disclosure statement is approved, it said it will seek approval of the reorganization plan from claimholders and from those who own a stake in the company.

The plan was the product of lengthy negotiations with each of the company's major creditors, Dangremond said. In a Chapter 11 proceeding, a company is protected while it works out arrangements with its creditors.
"We believe that the creditors' committee and the other major holders of Forstmann's debt are prepared to support the plan," he said.
The company said the plan primarily involves converting general, unsecured claims against it into 100 percent of the reorganized Forstmann's common stock.
Substantially all of the secured claims against the company will be either refinanced or reinstated, it said.

Holders of Forstmann's existing preferred and common stock will receive warrants to buy two percent of the common stock of the reorganized company, excercisable within two years from bankruptcy emergence.
The company said the bankruptcy court has approved a $110 million financing it will receive from BankAmerica Business Credit Inc, a BankAmerica Corp unit, upon its exit from bankruptcy.
